title: Turning a blind eye
goal: Name facts, claims and possibilities with a whole clause, use the -mAzlIk idioms, and recognize words built with -GAn, -GIn, -(I)m, -(I)ntI, -sAl, -DAş, -(y)IcI and -mAn.

intro.text: A noun can take a whole clause as its content: *dünyanın döndüğü gerçeği* (the fact that the earth turns), *yağmur yağması ihtimali* (the chance of rain). The head noun takes `-(s)I`, as in a compound. *Bilmezlikten gelmek* is **to pretend not to know**.

vocab.en: effect, influence (etkisi altında: under the influence of)
to ignore, to turn a blind eye to

exercises.question: Which phrase means **the news that the observatory would be closed**?

why.1: Without `-(s)I`, the clause reads as a relative clause describing *haber*, like *okuduğum haber* (the news I read). When the clause is the content of the news, the head noun takes `-(s)I`: *haberi*.
why.2: *Gözlemevini kapatacak haber* is **the news that will close the observatory**: the news does the closing.

exercises.explain: Clause + head noun with `-(s)I`, as in a compound: *kapatılacağı haberi*, **the news that it would be closed**.

exercises.text: Yarın yağmur yağması ___ yüksek; gözlemi erteleyelim mi?
exercises.en: The chance of rain tomorrow is high; shall we postpone the observation?

accept: ihtimali
olasılığı

reject.why: The head noun takes `-(s)I`, as in a compound: *yağmur yağması ihtimali*.
*İhtimal* is a loanword with front suffixes, like *saat*: *ihtimali*.

exercises.explain: A possibility is named by a `-mA` clause: *yağmur yağması ihtimali*. *Olasılığı* is the more formal synonym.

exercises.prompt: Dünyanın güneşin etrafında döndüğü gerçeği uzun süre kabul edilmedi.
accept: The fact that the earth goes around the sun was not accepted for a long time.
The fact that earth [goes|revolves|turns|moves] [around|round] the sun was not accepted for a long time.
The fact that the earth goes round the sun was not accepted for a long time.
The fact that the earth revolves [around|round] the sun was not accepted for a long time.
The fact that the earth turns [around|round] the sun was not accepted for a long time.
The fact that the earth moves [around|round] the sun was not accepted for a long time.
For a long time, the fact that (the) earth [goes|revolves|turns|moves] [around|round] the sun was not accepted.
For a long time, [people|they] did not accept the fact that (the) earth [goes|revolves|turns|moves] [around|round] the sun.
It was not accepted for a long time that (the) earth [goes|revolves|turns|moves] [around|round] the sun.
exercises.explain: *-DIğI gerçeği*: the clause is the content of *gerçek* (fact). *Etrafında* (around) is a place noun ([A2 unit 9](gp-place-nouns)).

exercises.prompt: We heard the news that the observatory would be closed.
accept: Gözlemevinin kapatılacağı haberini duyduk.
Gözlemevinin kapatılacağı haberini aldık.
Gözlemevinin kapanacağı haberini [duyduk|aldık].
Biz gözlemevinin [kapatılacağı|kapanacağı] haberini [duyduk|aldık].

reject.why: *Haber* is the definite object of *duyduk*, so after `-(s)I` it takes the accusative with the pronominal n: *haberini*.

exercises.explain: *Kapatılacağı haberi* (the news that it would be closed) + accusative: *haberini duyduk*.

exercises.text: Ona soruyu üç kez sordum, ama ___ geldi.
exercises.en: I asked him the question three times, but he pretended not to hear.

accept: duymazlıktan

reject.why: *Duymadan* is **without hearing**. **To pretend not to hear** is the idiom *duymazlıktan gelmek*.
*Gelmek* here takes the ablative: *duymazlıktan gelmek*, literally **to come from not-hearing**.

exercises.explain: `-mAz` + `-lIk` + ablative + *gelmek*: *duymazlıktan gelmek*, **to pretend not to hear**. Likewise *bilmezlikten* and *anlamazlıktan gelmek*.
`-(I)m` makes a noun of an act or its result: *ölç-üm* (measurement), *seç-im* (election), *doğ-um* (birth). Its vowel follows harmony: ü after ö.

exercises.prompt: There was a disagreement between my colleague and me.
accept: Meslektaşımla aramızda bir anlaşmazlık vardı.
Meslektaşımla aramızda anlaşmazlık vardı.
Meslektaşım ile aramızda (bir) anlaşmazlık vardı.
Benimle meslektaşım arasında (bir) anlaşmazlık vardı.
Meslektaşımla aramda (bir) anlaşmazlık vardı.
Meslektaşımla (bir) anlaşmazlık yaşadık.
exercises.explain: *Aramızda*: **between us**, with the possessive of *biz*, since you are one of the two. *Anlaş-mazlık* is the state of not agreeing.

exercises.prompt: Yeni meslektaşım çok çalışkan ama biraz unutkan.
accept: My new colleague is very hard-working but a bit forgetful.
My new colleague is very hard-working but a little forgetful.
My new colleague is very hard-working but slightly forgetful.
My new colleague is very hard-working but somewhat forgetful.
My new colleague is very hard-working but rather forgetful.
My new colleague is very hardworking but [a bit|a little|slightly|somewhat|rather] forgetful.
My new colleague is very diligent but [a bit|a little|slightly|somewhat|rather] forgetful.
My new colleague is very industrious but [a bit|a little|slightly|somewhat|rather] forgetful.
exercises.explain: *Çalış-kan*, *unut-kan*: `-GAn` turns a verb into a trait, **someone who tends to**. Not *çalışan*, which is **working** or **employee**.

exercises.question: How do you write **someone who shares your profession**?

why.1: `-DAş` keeps its a even after front vowels: *meslektaş*, *dindaş*, *gönüldaş*.
why.2: After the voiceless k, the d turns into t: *meslek-taş*, as in *yurt-taş*.

exercises.task: A colleague ignored a mistake in a report. Write three or four sentences about what happened. Use at least one clause + head noun (*-DIğI gerçeği*, *-DIğI iddiası*, *-mAsI ihtimali*, *-mAsI tehlikesi*) and one `-mAzlIk` idiom.
models: Raporda bir hata olduğu gerçeğini herkes biliyordu. Ama Murat Bey bilmezlikten geldi ve raporu olduğu gibi gönderdi. Sonuçların yanlış anlaşılması tehlikesi vardı; bu yüzden ben müdüre haber verdim.
Meslektaşım, ölçümlerin eksik olduğu iddiasını görmezden geldi. Ona iki kez yazdım, ama duymazlıktan geldi. Raporun bu hâliyle yayımlanması ihtimali beni çok endişelendiriyor.
checklist: A head noun with `-(s)I` after its clause: *olduğu gerçeği*, *yanlış anlaşılması tehlikesi*
`-DIk` before facts and claims, `-mA` before possibilities and dangers
The case the main verb needs on the head noun: *gerçeğini biliyordu*, *iddiasını görmezden geldi*
